exchanges.question: Not an analyst exchange: this numbered block is the scripted management discussion that functions as the prepared remarks. Seibert presents Q2 results, segment results, industry outlook and fiscal 2026 guidance, Norwood gives opening comments, and Seibert then asks Beal and Norwood about the quarter, tariffs, ag markets by region, construction markets, new and used inventory, the guidance bridge and ag innovation, before Norwood closes.
exchanges.answer: Seibert reported net sales growth of 5% and an equipment operations margin of 16.9%, net sales and revenues of $13.369 billion, equipment net sales of $11.778 billion and net income of $1.773 billion or $6.55 per diluted share, with results helped by a $272 million recovery of IEEPA tariff refund claims that lifted margins by nearly 2.5 points; fiscal 2026 net income guidance is unchanged at $4.5 billion-$5 billion, effective tax rate 24%-26%, equipment operations cash flow $4.5 billion-$5.5 billion, Financial Services raised to $860 million, PPA sales down 5%-10% with 11%-13% margin (unchanged), SAT up approximately 15% with 13.5%-15% margin, and C&F raised to up approximately 20% with margin raised to 10%-12%; the South America industry outlook was cut to down about 15% from down 5%. Norwood said Large Ag is operating below trough, SAT is progressing toward mid-cycle and C&F is slightly above mid-cycle, all with double-digit margins, top line should grow more than 5% this year toward the 2030 Leap Ambitions, and the baseline view remains that 2026 is the bottom of the ag cycle despite the Iran conflict. Beal said the direct tariff run rate remains approximately $1.2 billion (about a 3% margin headwind) after IEEPA was invalidated and Section 122 and 232 changed, or approximately $900 million net of refunds; year-over-year direct tariff expense was about $200 million of Q2 headwind; Norwood said implied net price realization is 1.5%-2% for the year, consistent with inflation ex-tariffs, with no surcharges, about 80% of U.S. complete goods sales produced in U.S. facilities with roughly 75% U.S.-sourced components, Deere-designed excavators now built in Kernersville, North Carolina after a $70 million expansion, and a $20 billion U.S. manufacturing commitment over 10 years. On markets, Beal said Brazil's tractor and combine industry declined about 15% in six months while Deere retail declined less, Brazilian growers plant in September and are exposed to spot input prices, U.S. policy support includes approved RVO, disaster relief payment factors raised from 35% to 70% and House passage of year-round E15 (roughly one-third of U.S. corn goes to ethanol); Norwood said the U.S. and Canada construction order book is up more than 60% since November to its highest since April 2024 with over 80% of production slots filled, nearly all production slots for the new excavator are spoken for after CONEXPO 2026 (over 140,000 contractors), and data center construction should top $100 billion in 2026 with double-digit growth in 2027. Beal said North American new high horsepower tractor and combine inventories are down more than 50% from the mid-2024 peak, used combines down mid-teens from the March 2024 peak, used tractors down mid-teens from peak and down low single digits sequentially, model year 2022-2023 8R tractors down around 45% from peak, used sprayers down approximately 30% and used planters roughly 50%; model year 2027 spring EOPs are just launching, Waterloo order books run well into the fourth quarter, Brazil will underproduce retail especially in combines, PPA and SAT price realization expectations were trimmed by approximately half a point, and Norwood expects slightly higher second-half revenue with Q4 above Q3 and the most favorable cost comparisons in Q4. On innovation, Beal cited six new 8R and 8RX models (440, 490 and 540 horsepower, JD14 engine), ExactDepth, FurrowVision, ExactShot with ExactRate, See & Spray expansion to wheat, barley and canola, See & Scout, Casa John Deere in Brazil (over 3,000 customers from over 25 countries, over 20 new products), Precision Essentials, Starlink connectivity with more than 12,500 JDLink Boost kits sold and 25% growth last quarter; Norwood added engaged acres up about 10% year over year, highly engaged acres growing faster, nearly 440,000 monthly active digital users, and $635 million returned to shareholders in the quarter.

exchanges.question: With construction sales growth far outpacing the up 5% industry forecast, is Deere seeing healthy industry growth and is it gaining a lot of share?
exchanges.answer: Beal said last year's underproduction in earthmoving, particularly in the front half, gives a natural lift as production aligns with retail this year, on top of industry growth of 5% in earthmoving and continued road building strength. Deere has also picked up share over the past 12 months, particularly the last six or so, following pricing adjustments at the end of last year.

exchanges.question: Can you break down the $272 million tariff refund between segments to understand the baseline margin in each business?
exchanges.answer: Beal said the full-year tariff expense run rate is unchanged at about $1.2 billion, split about 45% Construction & Forestry, about a third Small Ag & Turf and about 20% large ag, a roughly 3 point full-year margin impact. The $272 million refund is about a point of full-year tailwind for equipment operations, split about 50% to C&F, about 30% to Small Ag & Turf and 20% to large ag.

exchanges.question: Since Deere has not priced to offset tariffs, what mitigation strategies has it pursued, what progress has been made over the last 12 months, and what more is to come?
exchanges.answer: Norwood said price realization is forecast at about 1.5%-2% for equipment operations, in line with general inflation ex-tariffs of about 1.5%-2%, so tariffs are margin dilutive; Deere is not surcharging customers given inconsistent tariff rates and is instead reducing exposure through resourcing, reshoring, exemption submissions and USMCA compliance, and he has full confidence tariffs will be largely countered through cost measures over coming periods. Beal added that in the back half of 2026 Deere laps both last year's tariff expense and associated inflation, and laps incentives taken in C&F and large ag, so price and production cost comps both improve and price-cost improves through the balance of the year.

exchanges.question: How would Deere frame downside risk to its regional ag outlooks given the abnormal geopolitical environment, and is there a historical period that serves as a reference for farmer behavior?
exchanges.answer: Beal said the industry is a couple of years into the downturn with very elevated fleet ages for high horsepower tractors and combines in North America and a much healthier used market, with model year 2022 and 2023 high horsepower tractors down about 45% from their peak a year ago; customer margin pressure has heightened with fertilizer, most acutely in Brazil, where the guide was cut. The baseline remains a 2027 recovery, with pace depending on policy, ag fundamentals and geopolitics. Seibert added the situation differs across Europe, the U.S. and Brazil: U.S. corn and soybean prices are up about 20% since August and U.S. farmers secured inputs ahead of planting, so their year looks a little better than at peak uncertainty in August.

exchanges.question: What order trends is Deere seeing in large ag seasonal products, and which regional trends stand out?
exchanges.answer: Beal said 2026 production for combines, sprayers and planters is set with this year's EOPs closed. The model year 2027 sprayer EOP opened at the beginning of May and runs through the end of August as a two-phase program, with planters opening at the beginning of June and running through the end of September. It is very early and should not be extrapolated, but everything seen so far supports the view that 2026 marks the bottom of the ag cycle.

exchanges.question: What See & Spray acreage is expected this year, how are retrofit orders tracking, what are Precision Essentials renewal rates for the 2025 cohort, and what list price increases accompany the advanced features in the EOP?
exchanges.answer: Beal said See & Spray covered 1 million acres in year one and 5 million acres globally last year, and the same customers are spraying more acres year-to-date than last year, with two years of demonstrated 50%-60% herbicide savings; See & Spray Green on Green was introduced at Casa John Deere for next year, crop coverage is expanding to wheat, barley and canola, and early 2027 EOP take rates exceed this year's. Seibert said Precision Essentials orders are trending well year over year and have brought more than 4,000, closer to 5,000, new customer organizations into Operations Center. Beal said Precision Essentials renewals remain in the 70% range overall while the second-year cohort renews at over 90%, and harvest settings automation utilization was over 60% in the Northern Hemisphere harvest and over 80% in Brazil. No acreage target, retrofit figure or list price detail was given.

exchanges.question: What is the cadence for 3Q and 4Q sales and margins, and are there any regional or segment items that could make the second half deviate from normal seasonality?
exchanges.answer: Beal said the back half will be higher than the front half with Q4 a bit higher than Q3. Large Ag Q4 will be stronger than Q3 because more Waterloo large tractor shipments to North America fall in the back half, which is abnormal but reflects how the order book built; Small Ag has normal seasonality with a step down in Q3 and another in Q4; C&F is fairly balanced with Q4 maybe a little stronger. Nothing specifically abnormal was called out.

exchanges.question: Why do large ag pricing expectations look more conservative than peers, and does that reflect higher discounting?
exchanges.answer: Beal said the quarter's downward price adjustment was driven by Brazil, but all regions are expected to be price positive in large ag; the full-year guide is 1%, with North America a bit better and the other two regions a little lower. Seibert added that second-half price will look better than the first half given prior discounting, and progress on used inventory from the incentives put in place supports the pricing mechanics.

exchanges.question: Is the $272 million IEEPA refund a true benefit versus the initial guide, or do other tariffs offset it back to $1.2 billion? And how does the expected price-cost improvement square with raw material, component and energy costs that appear to be getting tougher?
exchanges.answer: Beal said the $1.2 billion is the unchanged run rate of tariff expense with puts and takes, the $272 million refund is new in the quarter, and net tariff cost will be more like $900 million this year. He agreed material inflation has come in over the last two or three months, but back-half comps improve as Deere laps the tariffs and indirect tariff inflation that arrived in the back half of last year. Norwood added that pricing is much more favorable in the back half so price-cost ratios improve meaningfully, and large ag factories will see better overhead absorption in Q4 as production rates are significantly higher given the heavier fourth-quarter large tractor order book.

exchanges.question: What sentiment and feedback are Deere and its North American dealers hearing on large ag, and how do they expect the spring early order program to play out as a first lens on 2027 capex?
exchanges.answer: Beal said the baseline is some level of recovery next year driven by fleet age and new and used inventory progress, and dealers feel it too: John Deere Financial trade wholesale (used equipment financed on dealer lots) is down over 15% year over year in portfolio size, freeing balance sheets for new sales. About a third of old crop still needs to be sold and higher commodity prices support that, though there is some caution on next year's input costs. Norwood said dealer feedback varies: dealers who acted early on used are most optimistic, a couple are even looking to add select used units, while others are more moderate depending on how aggressively they managed inventory.

exchanges.question: Are South American market share gains coming from the existing product portfolio or from the new products being rolled out there?
exchanges.answer: Beal said share in tractors and combines has risen on a steady, fairly linear path over the last decade and a half, supported by new products and technologies, an outstanding dealer channel and more localization. Last spring's record launch was topped this year with new combines, sprayers, planters, See & Spray and Starlink connectivity, harvest settings automation utilization in Brazil is the highest in the globe, and Deere is extremely bullish on the region.
